Case Study · 03 · DutchDrops

A premium
position, earned

DutchDrops is an e-commerce agency in the Netherlands. I led the end-to-end website redesign: site architecture, user journeys and a consistent interface system across every key touchpoint, moving the brand to a more premium position while making it clearer to use.

Role
Lead designerUI/UX strategy and interface system
Scope
Full site, six pagesArchitecture, hierarchy, UI
Also
Brand bookRedesigned alongside the site
Status
DeliveredAwaiting client launch
Approach

Structure first

The brief was a more premium presence. Most of that came from restructuring rather than restyling: a clearer architecture, a tighter content hierarchy and one interface system applied consistently across all six pages.

Brand book

The identity system the interface was built on, redesigned alongside it.

Hover to pause · click a spread to enlarge
01

One letter, twice

The mark is two D forms in one: the outer shape and the counter inside it. A single construction that reads at signage scale and at favicon size.

02

The shape carries the brand

That same quarter-round crops the imagery across the system. It is what makes a poster, a billboard and a homepage read as one brand without a logo on every surface.

03

Two typefaces, clear roles

Roboto for display, Inter for everything functional, on a defined scale. The site inherits it directly, so brand and interface never drift apart.
